static_diagnosis.fact: Every in/name record resolves its full parent prefix plus dot and suffix into a new Python string. The accumulated name_bytes estimate starts with list/empty-string sizes and adds sys.getsizeof(resolved)+16 for each candidate name. The32MiB NAME_CAP check throws before appending the name that would exceed the estimate.

This is an independent accounting budget for expanded-name retention, not the256MiB observed-RSS stop and not the120s deadline. It is an estimate with a16B per-name allowance, not an exact allocator/heap measurement. It includes the name whose estimate causes failure even though that name has not yet been appended.

The name table is maintained for all names encountered in the dependency-closed export, before any declaration's known-namespace/origin classification. Repeated full prefixes are stored in separate resolved strings. The error therefore reflects this scanner representation's fixed capacity being exhausted.

The exception bypassed EOF/full SHA comparison and successful global/segment/root output. The failure handler only serialized the error, elapsed and sampled peak RSS. It did not preserve the terminating name, byte offset, number of names, partial counters or rankings.

positive_support: Only that this particular name-expanding metadata scanner hit its predeclared32MiB name-accounting budget after about20s, with observed own RSS53.55MiB and a real child nonzero. No rescanning is authorized by this report.
